title: Production of Extracellular Matrix Fibers via Sacrificial Hollow Fiber Membrane Cell Culture
protocol: Weigh 70 g of polysulfone pellets in a weigh boat using an analytical balance.
Transfer 314 mL of N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP) to a clean borosilicate flask.
Place a stir bar in the flask with NMP and place flask onto stirrer.
Set the stirrer to a moderate rate of rotation.
Use a dry funnel to slowly insert the prepared 70 g of polysulfone into the flask with NMP.
Allow the polymer “dope” solution to stir for three days at room temperature, or until homogenized.
Gently flow acetone through the inlet and outlet of the spinneret.
Collect any acetone and residual polymer in a glass beaker for disposal.
Secure the upper body of the spinneret with the needle facing upward in a table vise.
Place the outlet (bottom) body of the spinneret onto the upper body.
Move the outlet body of the spinneret laterally while holding the upper body fixed on the vise until the spinneret needle is directly in the center of the outlet body.
Carefully and slowly reinsert the screws connecting the two bodies of the spinneret while ensuring that the needle visible at the spinneret outlet remains centered.
Prepare a “bore solution” containing 45 mL of N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone and 255 mL of deionized water, forming a 15% mixture of NMP with deionized water.
Mount a concentric hollow fiber membrane spinneret 8 cm above the surface of a room-temperature tap water bath.
Connect the polymer inlet of the spinneret to one steel pressure vessel.
Connect the bore inlet of the spinneret to another steel pressure vessel.
Ensure both vessels have check valves at their outlets.
Connect each of the pressure vessels to the regulators of separate N2 gas cylinders.
Use a funnel to insert the prepared dope solution (~315 mL) into the pressure vessel connected to the polymer inlet of the spinneret.
Ensure that the top of the vessel is tightly sealed.
Use a funnel to insert the prepared bore solution (300 mL) into the pressure vessel connected to the spinneret inlet.
Tightly seal the top of the vessel.
Open the check valve for the bore vessel first, then open the polymer vessel second.
Pressurize both vessels to 1 PSI.
Visually confirm that both polymer and bore solutions are exiting the spinneret, forming a continuous white filament in the water bath.
Use long forceps to guide the nascent fiber under the rollers in the center of the bath.
Wind the nascent fiber around a rotating wheel connected to a motor at a rate of approximately two meters per minute.
Make minor adjustments to the regulators or take-up wheel speed as needed until steady-state flow is achieved.
Ensure the nascent fiber forms a 90° angle with the surface of the water bath.
Close the N2 cylinder regulators and pressure vessel check valves after all polymer and bore solution has been extruded.
Disengage the take-up wheel motor.
Remove the prepared hollow fiber membranes from the spinneret.
Place the membranes into a deionized water bath for three days, exchanging deionized water once per day to remove residual solvent.
Sterilize the hollow fiber membranes by autoclaving them at 121 °C for 30 minutes or by immersing them in 70% ethanol for one day.
Treat the hollow fiber membranes with a 20 µg/mL solution of bovine plasma fibronectin in PBS (pH = 7.4) to promote cell attachment.
Weigh 1 mg of powdered bovine plasma fibronectin and dissolve it in 1 mL of sterile PBS (pH = 7.4).
Incubate the 1 mg/mL bovine plasma fibronectin solution for 30 minutes.
Add the fibronectin solution to 49 mL of sterile PBS.
Incubate the hollow fiber membranes in the prepared fibronectin solution at 37 °C with 5% CO2 for 1 hour.
Recollect the fibronectin solution and store it in a sterile 50 mL conical centrifuge tube at 4 °C.
Cut the fibers to a desired length of less than 6 cm using sterile microscissors.
Seed fibroblast cells directly into the lumina of the hollow fiber membranes at a density of 100,000 cells per fiber using a 21-gauge needle with a 1 mL syringe.
Prepare the cell suspension for loading in the syringe at a density of 100,000 cells for every 30 microliters of medium.
Place six seeded fibers into a 6 cm diameter Petri dish.
Allow the seeded fibers to incubate at 37 °C with 5% CO2 for five minutes.
Remove seeded fibers from incubation.
Culture fibers for up to 3 weeks in DMEM/F-12 containing final concentrations of 50 µg/mL L-ascorbic acid and 150 µg/mL L-ascorbic acid 2-phosphate, 5 ng/mL TGF-β1, and 1% penicillin-streptomycin.
Exchange cell medium every two days.
Place cultured fibers into individual scintillation vials using forceps.
Add up to 5 mL of NMP into each vial using a glass pipette.
Immerse hollow fibers in NMP, performing three exchanges of NMP.
Aspirate old NMP slowly using a 1 mL pipette to prevent tearing of extracted ECM.
Remove NMP and rinse the resulting ECM thread three times in deionized water.
Cut a 1/32-inch thick sheet of silicone rubber to a length of 3 inches, width of 1 inch, and cut an 8 mm by 4 mm rectangular mold in the center.
Place the prepared piece of rubber onto a standard microscopy slide.
Autoclave at 121 °C for 30 minutes.
Lay each ECM fiber side by side in the silicone mold until there is no visible open space.
Place the mold into a 50 mL conical centrifuge tube.
Freeze the mold at -80°C until completely frozen.
Lyophilize the frozen ECM mesh overnight or until completely dry.
Store the lyophilized mesh at 4°C until ready for decellularization.
Prepare a solution of 1% (w/w%) sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) in deionized water.
Incubate extracted extracellular matrix in the mold with 1% SDS for 24 hours at room temperature on a rocker with gentle agitation.
Rinse the extracted extracellular matrix three times in sterile phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) with gentle agitation, using 3 mL of PBS per rinse.
Weigh 1.54 g of Tris HCl, 308 mg of MgCl2, and 56 mg of CaCl2 in separate weigh boats.
Combine Tris HCl, MgCl2, and CaCl2 with 1 L of deionized water in a large flask with a stir bar and stir until all components are dissolved.
Sterile filter the digestion buffer with a 0.22 µm filter into a sterile 1 L borosilicate bottle and store at 4°C.
Prepare 5 mL of DNAse/RNAse digestion solution by weighing 0.125 mg (50 kU) of DNAse I in a weigh boat and adding it to the digestion buffer.
Add 75 µL of RNAse A stock solution to the digestion buffer.
Fill each mold with the digestion solution and incubate at 4 °C for 6 hours.
Aspirate the digestion solution and rinse three times in sterile PBS.
Aspirate the PBS and incubate scaffolds overnight in 10% penicillin-streptomycin in PBS at 4°C.
Aspirate the penicillin-streptomycin and rinse scaffolds three times in sterile PBS.
Place the mold into a 50 mL conical centrifuge tube and freeze at -80°C.
Lyophilize the decellularized ECM mesh overnight or until completely dry.
Transfer the lyophilized scaffolds within a biosafety hood to a sterile container at 4°C pending use.
